faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions about Otolaryngology and Rhinoplasty
faq.question1: When should I see an otolaryngologist?
faq.answer1:
It is recommended to seek care when you experience:

Persistent nasal obstruction
Snoring or sleep apnea
Frequent sinusitis
Throat pain or recurrent infections
Voice changes
Dizziness or hearing loss
Swelling or lumps in the neck
faq.question2: What is an otolaryngology consultation like?
faq.answer2:
The consultation begins with a detailed clinical interview, evaluating:

Current symptoms
Medical and surgical history
Allergies
Habits (smoking, medication use, etc.)
History of recurrent infections or respiratory problems

Afterwards, a specialized physical examination of the ears, nose, and throat is performed.

Depending on the case, additional studies may be ordered such as:

Imaging studies (X-rays or CT scans)
Allergy tests
Hearing tests
Cultures or specific analyses
faq.question3: How is a rhinoplasty evaluation conducted?
faq.answer3:
The evaluation includes:

Comprehensive facial analysis (proportions, symmetry, and facial harmony)
Functional assessment of nasal breathing
Study of the septum and internal structures
Clinical photographs
Detailed explanation of realistic expectations and possible results
faq.question4: When will I see the results?
faq.answer4:
The change is visible as soon as the splint is removed (approximately 7–10 days).

However:

Swelling progressively decreases during the first 3 months.
The most refined results can be seen between 6 and 12 months.
Patience is key, as the nose is a structure that heals and reduces swelling gradually

ear.title_h1: Balance Disorders: Vertigo and Dizziness - Why Do They Occur and When to See a Specialist?
ear.intro_text: Feeling like everything is spinning around you or losing stability is one of the most common reasons for consultation with Dr. Lumbán. Understanding how the balance system works helps identify symptoms and seek medical attention.
ear.what_is_vertigo_text: Vertigo is a balance disorder characterized by a false sensation of movement, usually described as if everything is spinning around you or as if you are spinning.
ear.vertigo_symptoms_title: During episodes, the following may occur:
ear.vertigo_cause: Vertigo is usually caused by an alteration of the vestibular system, located in the inner ear, which controls balance.
ear.vertigo_types_text: For diagnosis, we classify vertigo into two main groups:
ear.vertigo_peripheral: Peripheral Vertigo: This is the most common type. It is caused by an alteration in the labyrinth or the vestibular nerve. It often includes auditory symptoms such as ringing or pressure in the ear.
ear.vertigo_central: Central Vertigo: This originates from alterations in the brain or brainstem. Instability is usually very pronounced and may include double vision.
ear.what_is_dizziness_text: Dizziness is a sensation of instability or 'empty head.' It may include impending fainting, cold sweating, paleness, nausea, and general discomfort.
ear.dizziness_note: Unlike vertigo, dizziness does not always involve a spinning sensation and may be related to circulatory, neurological, or metabolic problems.
ear.balance_system_title: How Does Our Balance Work? The Role of the Inner Ear
ear.balance_system_text: Balance does not depend on a single organ but on several systems coordinated by the brain.
ear.balance_systems_list:
Vestibular system (inner ear)
Visual system
Musculoskeletal and proprioceptive system
ear.brain_balance: The brain combines information from these systems to maintain posture and body orientation.
ear.inner_ear_title: The Inner Ear and the Vestibular System
ear.inner_ear_text: Inside the inner ear there is a structure called the labyrinth, made up of bone and soft tissues filled with fluid. This system detects head movements and body position.
ear.semicircular_canals_text: They are three tubes filled with fluid that detect head rotations. Inside them, a gelatinous structure called the cupula acts like a 'ship's sail' that moves with the fluid, and sensory cells with small extensions called stereocilia.
ear.head_movement4: A nerve signal is generated to the brain indicating the direction of movement.
ear.otolithic_text: These structures inform the brain and detect gravity. Thanks to them, the brain knows whether you are sitting, lying down, or moving sideways.
ear.balance_failure: If any of these signals fail, a balance disorder appears.
ear.balance_disorder_symptoms_text: In addition to the spinning sensation, balance disorders may manifest as:
ear.symptom1: Difficulty walking in a straight line or staggering.
ear.symptom3: Feeling of floating or impending fall.
ear.causes_title: Frequent Causes of Vertigo and Dizziness
ear.causes_text: Balance problems can originate from multiple factors:
ear.common_diseases_title: Most Common Diseases Related to Vertigo
ear.bppv_text: Occurs when small calcium crystals (otoliths) detach and float in the ear canals, causing brief but intense vertigo when moving the head.
ear.labyrinthitis_text: Inflammation or infection of the inner ear, usually associated with viral respiratory infections. It can cause:
ear.meniere_text: It is characterized by recurrent episodes of:
ear.meniere_note: It is related to alterations of the fluid within the labyrinth.
ear.fistula_text: A fluid leak in the inner ear, common after trauma or sudden pressure changes.
ear.warning_signs_title: Warning Signs: When to See an Otolaryngologist?
ear.warning_signs_text: If dizziness or vertigo is accompanied by the following symptoms:
ear.warning1: Severe headache or sudden neck pain.
ear.warning4: Weakness or numbness in arms or legs.
ear.warning_note: These symptoms may indicate a serious neurological cause
ear.self_assessment_title: Self-Assessment: Should You Consult Dr. Lumbán?
ear.self_assessment_text: If you answered 'yes' to any of these questions, it is recommended to have a professional evaluation:
ear.question1: Do you feel like the room is spinning?
ear.question2: Do you lose balance and fall frequently?
ear.question3: Do you feel like you are going to faint when standing up?
ear.question4: Does your vision become blurry during episodes?
ear.self_assessment_note: Vertigo and dizziness should not be considered normal symptoms. Although many causes are benign, some may indicate diseases that require specialized diagnosis.
ear.conclusion: An appropriate otolaryngological evaluation allows identifying the origin of the problem and offering effective treatments that significantly improve quality of life.

ear.balance_description1: Our balance is a complex interaction that requires strong communication between our ears, eyes, and the sense of touch based on the perception of our feet, muscles, and joints. To maintain our center of gravity, our central nervous system must receive these three signals and then correctly transmit them to the brain.
ear.balance_description2: When signals from our senses do not reach the cerebellum, or reach it with the wrong message, we experience this lack of communication as a loss of balance, dizziness.
ear.balance_description3: A balance disorder can sometimes be a symptom of other medical conditions. Proper medical care, including a complete medical history and evaluation of the balance system, is important to identify the cause and provide appropriate treatment options.
ear.vertigo_description: It is the perception of spinning, movement, or rotation of either oneself or the surrounding environment. It is usually episodic rather than constant.
ear.imbalance_description: It is a sensation of instability or loss of balance, whether at rest or when walking, or both. It is often described as a feeling of 'being on a boat.' These symptoms may or may not be accompanied by a feeling of clogged ears, hearing loss, or ringing in the ears.
ear.cause_fluid_buildup: Fluid buildup in the inner ear. Ménière's disease
ear.evaluation_text: If you have balance problems or dizziness, we will complete a comprehensive evaluation. Our balance laboratory can perform a series of tests to help diagnose and treat your problem.
ear.vestibular_rehab_description: "Vestibular rehabilitation" is a series of exercises for balance recovery. They can be performed at home or by an audiologist, and each rehabilitation program is specifically designed to correct the patient's balance disorders.
ear.canal_repositioning_description: Many cases of vertigo can be resolved with a simple positioning procedure in the office. Canal repositioning maneuvers are treatments that guide the patient through a series of head and body positions designed to move loosened otoconia (crystals) back into the balance organ.
ear.lifestyle_description: Caffeine, salt, alcohol, nicotine, and dehydration can all have a considerable impact on the sense of balance. Dr. Lumbán will provide you with medications and recommendations about diet and daily habits so that your balance problems can continue to be controlled at home.

hearing-loss.title_h1: Hearing Loss: Everything You Need to Know About Your Ears with an Otolaryngologist
hearing-loss.intro_text: Hearing loss is considered disabling when it exceeds 35 decibels (dB) in the ear with better hearing ability. This condition can range from mild to profound, affecting one or both ears, making it difficult to understand conversations or detect loud sounds.
hearing-loss.gradual_text: A key issue with hearing loss is that it is usually gradual. Because it develops slowly over years, the patient often only becomes aware of the problem when it has already advanced significantly.
hearing-loss.classification_title: Classification and Types of Hearing Loss
hearing-loss.classification_text: Hearing loss, also known as hearing impairment, is classified according to the area of the auditory system that is affected:
hearing-loss.conductive_text: This occurs when there is an obstacle preventing sound from reaching the sensory structures of the inner ear. The problem may be located in the external ear canal, the eardrum, or the middle ear.
hearing-loss.conductive_note: It makes sounds seem muffled. This type of hearing loss can often be corrected through medical or surgical intervention.
hearing-loss.conductive_cause1: fluid in the middle ear due to colds or allergies
hearing-loss.conductive_cause3: Eustachian tube dysfunction (a narrow tube connecting the middle ear to the throat)
hearing-loss.sensorineural_text: This is the most common type of permanent hearing loss. It occurs when sound reaches the inner ear but cannot be translated into nerve impulses, or the nerve impulses are not carried to the brain. It is generally not repairable through medical or surgical intervention.
hearing-loss.sensorineural_causes_title: Some possible causes of this type of hearing loss include:
hearing-loss.mixed_text: This is a combination of the two previous types. It can be caused by severe head trauma, chronic infection, or a genetic disorder.
hearing-loss.mixed_example: An example of mixed hearing loss would be if a person who normally has sensorineural hearing loss also developed an ear infection.
hearing-loss.specific_causes_title: Specific Causes and Common Hearing Loss Pathologies
hearing-loss.specific_causes_text: In addition to the general types, there are specific conditions that Dr. Lumbán frequently evaluates:
hearing-loss.cerumen_text: Sometimes wax accumulates in the ear canal and, in some cases, can completely block it. This often happens with hearing aid use, as the mold or casing tends to compress cerumen in the ear canal, which can lead to the formation of plugs that substantially reduce hearing.
hearing-loss.noise_text: Exposure to extreme noise (such as a firearm or nearby explosion) can cause sudden hearing loss, known as acoustic trauma. Hearing loss caused by acoustic trauma usually disappears within a day (unless the shockwave has also injured the eardrum or middle ear).
hearing-loss.noise_note: However, it is long-term exposure to noise that causes most noise-induced hearing loss.
hearing-loss.infections_title: Ear Infections (especially in children and young adults)
hearing-loss.infections_text: Otitis and Cholesteatoma: Infections can be acute (from bacteria from the pharynx) or chronic (from eardrum perforation). Chronic otitis can lead to cholesteatoma, a mass of cells with benign tumor-like behavior that requires specialized attention.
hearing-loss.otosclerosis_text: It is a middle ear disease where bone growth around the stapes prevents the ossicles from vibrating properly, making sound transmission difficult.
hearing-loss.warning_signs_title: How Do I Know If I'm Losing My Hearing? (Warning Signs)
hearing-loss.warning_signs_text: If you or a family member present the following signs, it's time to schedule a consultation with Dr. Lumbán:
hearing-loss.warning1: Difficulty understanding specific words during a conversation
hearing-loss.warning2: Frequently asking for words to be repeated
hearing-loss.warning4: Avoiding social situations due to difficulty hearing others
hearing-loss.warning5: Problems following conversation in groups or in the presence of background noise
hearing-loss.warning6: Noises in the ear such as ringing, roaring, whistling, buzzing, etc.
hearing-loss.degrees_text: To measure severity, specialists use the decibel scale (dB HL)
hearing-loss.aging_text: Older people often experience a progressive decrease in hearing called presbycusis. Statistics show a notable increase over the years:
hearing-loss.aging_stat1: 45 to 54 years: 5% have disabling hearing loss.
hearing-loss.aging_stat2: 55 to 64 years: The rate increases to 10%.
hearing-loss.aging_stat4: 75 years or older: Up to 55% of the population is affected.
hearing-loss.prevention_title: Prevention: How to Care for Your Ears?
hearing-loss.prevention_text: Limiting exposure to loud noises is the best prevention strategy. It is essential to control both the duration and intensity of sound.
hearing-loss.protection_text: If you regularly find yourself in noisy environments, strict protective measures will be necessary:
hearing-loss.protection2: Protective earmuffs: Especially those filled with glycerin that completely cover the ear.
hearing-loss.protection3: Safety rule: Any noise above 85 decibels (dB) can cause damage if exposure is prolonged.
hearing-loss.cta_appointment_text: If you or a family member begin to have difficulty understanding conversations or hearing clearly, we invite you to schedule your otolaryngology consultation with Dr. Jaime Lumbán. Our goal is to find a personalized solution to the hearing problem and prevent future complications.
hearing-loss.about_subtitle: To hear what you've lost, have your hearing thoroughly evaluated.
hearing-loss.stat_text: At any given time, about 30 million Americans are affected by hearing loss. Hearing loss disproportionately affects adults. And while it is more common among older adults, hearing loss is also a fact of life for adults in their 40s and 50s, not just for those over 65.
hearing-loss.gradual_description: A key issue with hearing loss is that it is usually gradual. While it can be sudden, hearing loss generally develops slowly over several years. The result is that most people with hearing loss are not aware of the extent of their problem.
hearing-loss.severity_text: It is also important to remember that hearing loss does not mean a total inability to hear. Hearing loss can be mild, moderate, severe, or total.
hearing-loss.sign1: Does not understand some words during conversation
hearing-loss.sign2: Frequently asks for words to be repeated
hearing-loss.sign3: Friends and family express concern about hearing
hearing-loss.sign5: Avoids social situations due to difficulty hearing others
hearing-loss.sign6: Problems following conversation in groups or in the presence of background noise
hearing-loss.sign7: Noises in the ear such as ringing, roaring, whistling, buzzing, etc.
hearing-loss.causes_title: Causes of Hearing Loss in Adults
hearing-loss.causes_text: Hearing loss in adults is most commonly the result of damage to the inner ear structure or the auditory nerve. It can be caused by aging, diseases, certain medications, injuries, infections, and noise exposure. While this type of hearing loss is not usually reversible, you can do something about it. The first thing to do is to have your hearing studied and determine the nature and extent of your hearing loss.

septoplasty.title_h1: Septoplasty: Nasal Septum Correction to Improve Breathing
septoplasty.intro_text: Nasal septum correction, known as septoplasty, is one of the most common procedures in otolaryngology. The nasal septum is the wall of bone and cartilage that divides the two nasal passages; when deviated, whether by birth or due to trauma, it can obstruct the passage of air.
septoplasty.common_text: Having a deviated septum is common, but if it is too deviated, it can obstruct airflow. This makes breathing difficult through one or both sides of the nose.
septoplasty.anatomy_title: Anatomy of Your Nose: How Does It Work?
septoplasty.anatomy_text: The nasal septum performs fundamental functions: it provides structural support to the nose and directs airflow in a balanced manner. The septum is made of thin bone in the back and cartilage in the front.
septoplasty.anatomy_note: A crooked septum can make breathing difficult. It can also cause snoring and sleep apnea.
septoplasty.symptom1: Persistent difficulty breathing through the nose.
septoplasty.symptom3: Sensation of nasal dryness or irritation.
septoplasty.surgery_title: Surgery: What Does a Septoplasty Involve?
septoplasty.surgery_text: Septoplasty aims to correct or reconstruct the deviated septum. Depending on the patient's needs, it can be performed alone or combined with rhinoplasty (aesthetic), turbinate surgery, or nasal valve surgery.
septoplasty.surgery_detail: During septoplasty, the septum is repositioned back to the center of the nose. To do this, Dr. Lumbán first reshapes, removes, or reinserts parts of the cartilage and bone in the correct position to open the airways.
septoplasty.incision_desc: It is achieved through a small incision inside the nostril, so it leaves no visible scars.
septoplasty.outpatient_desc: It is a procedure that usually takes less than an hour and does not require hospitalization.
septoplasty.recovery_desc: The vast majority of patients report minimal pain and can return to desk work within 3 to 5 days.
septoplasty.advanced_technique_text: Dr. Lumbán does not use nasal packing that blocks the passage of air after surgery. This allows the patient to leave the hospital breathing without obstruction, from the very first moment.
septoplasty.benefit1: Improved Breathing: Restores airflow, improving not only breathing but also sleep quality.
septoplasty.benefit2: Treatment for Apnea: Used as an auxiliary treatment in patients with sleep apnea, improving rest quality.
septoplasty.benefit3: Sports Performance: Beneficial for athletes who need adequate airflow during physical activity.
septoplasty.benefit4: Improved Sleep: Patients who previously breathed through their mouth while sleeping now enjoy natural nasal breathing.
septoplasty.differences_title: Main Differences Between Septoplasty and Rhinoplasty
septoplasty.differences_text: It is essential to distinguish between septoplasty and rhinoplasty, as both are surgical interventions on the nose but with different objectives.
septoplasty.differences_note: Septoplasty focuses on the functioning of the nasal septum, while rhinoplasty deals with the aesthetics of the nose.
septoplasty.differences_combined: Sometimes, both procedures can be combined to address both functional and aesthetic problems.
septoplasty.recovery_evolution_title: Evolution and Final Results of Septoplasty: What to Expect?
septoplasty.recovery_day1: First days: Mild swelling and congestion are normal, which decrease significantly by the end of the first week.
septoplasty.recovery_day10: At 10 days: Most patients resume their daily activities with basic precautions.
septoplasty.recovery_complete: Complete recovery: Tissue usually feels fully restored between 4 and 6 weeks.
septoplasty.recovery_note: Although respiratory improvement is evident soon, total septum stability and definitive tissue changes can take 3 to 6 months, or even up to a year to fully consolidate.

sinusitis.hero_subtitle: Specialized treatment for acute and chronic sinusitis
sinusitis.title_h1: Acute and Chronic Sinusitis: What is the Best Specialized Treatment?
sinusitis.intro_text: Sinusitis refers to inflammation within the nose, specifically the paranasal sinus cavities. It is classified as acute (short-term symptoms lasting 1-12 weeks) and chronic sinusitis (longer-lasting symptoms, 12 weeks or more).
sinusitis.intro_text2: This common condition prevents proper mucus drainage, causing nasal congestion, difficulty breathing, and tenderness or swelling around the eyes.
sinusitis.cause1: Infections: Frequent colds or other viral or bacterial infections affecting the sinuses.
sinusitis.cause2: Anatomical problems: Internal obstructions such as deviated nasal septum, nasal polyps, or tumors.
sinusitis.symptom1: Nasal congestion: Difficulty breathing due to inflammation and mucus buildup.
sinusitis.symptom2: Purulent discharge: Thick yellow or green mucus.
sinusitis.symptom3: Nasal drip: Constant flow of discolored mucus.
sinusitis.symptom4: Post-nasal drip: Sensation of mucus and discomfort in the back of the throat.
sinusitis.symptom5: Pain and pressure: Tenderness and swelling in eyes, cheeks, forehead, and throat.
sinusitis.diagnosis_text: Dr. Lumbán will conduct a comprehensive evaluation, including a detailed medical history, ENT examination (Complete evaluation of ears, nose, throat, larynx, and neck). This procedure is easily performed in the office with minimal discomfort, providing an accurate diagnosis, especially in cases of sinusitis.
sinusitis.treatment_text: Acute sinusitis is usually treated with antibiotics, anti-inflammatories, nasal decongestants, and corticosteroids (oral or injectable). If symptoms persist, advanced intervention may be required:
sinusitis.balloon_text: A minimally invasive procedure that helps eliminate trapped mucus by dilating the nasal passages.
sinusitis.cens_text: Indicated for patients with refractory inflammation (unresponsive to medical treatment), significant nasal obstruction, or anatomical abnormalities.
sinusitis.cens_note: This surgery prioritizes preservation of sinus function while restoring proper drainage. It is typically performed under general anesthesia on an outpatient basis (no hospitalization required).
sinusitis.cta_final: Breathe freely again. If conventional treatments haven't worked, it's time for a specialized evaluation. Dr. Lumbán offers minimally invasive solutions to help you return to your routine without discomfort. Schedule your evaluation today
sinusitis.stat_text: Sinusitis is one of the most common medical conditions requiring treatment annually in the United States. Generally speaking, sinusitis refers to inflammation of the sinus cavities, and is classified as acute sinusitis (short-term symptoms, anywhere from 1-12 weeks) and chronic sinusitis (longer-term symptoms, 12 weeks or more).
sinusitis.inflammation_text: While sinus inflammation is most often thought of as infectious (viral and bacterial), inflammation can also occur due to non-infectious processes, such as allergies, tobacco, or environmental irritants.
sinusitis.cold_text: The common cold is actually viral rhinosinusitis (nasal and sinus inflammation), which the body's own immune mechanisms typically resolve in 7-10 days.
sinusitis.diagnosis_viral_text: The vast majority (98%) of acute rhinosinusitis is viral. The only accurate indicator of the transition from viral rhinosinusitis to bacterial disease is symptom duration. As a rule of thumb, if rhinosinusitis symptoms are neither better nor worse after 10-14 days, bacterial infection is more likely and antibiotics are indicated.
sinusitis.diagnosis_evaluation_text: Dr. Lumbán will conduct a comprehensive evaluation, including a detailed medical history, ENT examination, and nasal endoscopy. This procedure is easily performed in the office with minimal discomfort and provides our physicians with a detailed assessment of nasal anatomy and inflammation status.
sinusitis.medical_treatment_text: When sinus inflammation is not resolved by the body's own mechanisms, or even with appropriate antibiotic therapy, then symptoms will persist and more intensive therapy may be indicated. This could include longer courses of antibiotics, concomitant use of decongestants and mucolytics, or possibly even anti-inflammatory steroids.
sinusitis.anatomical_text: Anatomical abnormalities may be detected, such as a deviated septum, nasal or sinus polyps, swelling, or abnormal secretions. These findings can help guide therapy and treatment response. CT imaging is used judiciously to fully evaluate the sinuses, providing information about the extent and distribution of sinus inflammation.
sinusitis.endoscopic_text: For patients whose inflammation is refractory and has little response to medical treatment, or who have significant nasal obstruction and/or anatomical abnormalities of the sinuses, surgery may be considered. Sinus surgery is performed endoscopically, prioritizing preservation of sinus function while restoring proper drainage, known as Functional Endoscopic Sinus Surgery (FESS).
sinusitis.endoscopic_note: It is most frequently performed under general anesthesia on an outpatient basis (i.e., same-day surgery). In some cases, CT imaging is used with image guidance technology, allowing real-time tracking of surgical instruments during the procedure.
sinusitis.risk_factors_text: If you suffer from frequent repeated sinus infections, or if you have truly chronic symptoms that do not respond to treatments, please make an appointment with Dr. Lumbán for a comprehensive evaluation. A complete history will be taken, an evaluation of nasal and sinus anatomy will be performed, and other factors that may need treatment will be identified, such as:
sinusitis.risk_tobacco_note: The harmful effects of tobacco use on nasal and sinus membranes cannot be overstated.
sinusitis.cta_chronic_text: Through endoscopic surgery, Dr. Lumbán can help you improve your health with minimal pain.

nasal-congestion.hero_subtitle: Specialized treatment for stuffy nose and breathing problems
nasal-congestion.title_h1: Nasal Congestion: Specialized Treatment for Stuffy Nose and Breathing Problems
nasal-congestion.intro_text: Nasal congestion occurs when the inside of the nose swells due to inflamed blood vessels.
nasal-congestion.intro_text2: The problem may also include rhinorrhea or runny nose. If excess mucus runs down the back of the throat (postnasal drip), it can cause coughing or sore throat.
nasal-congestion.warning_text: Untreated nasal congestion can lead to hearing problems, chronic fatigue, insomnia, headaches. It can also increase the frequency and volume of snoring, potentially leading to Sleep Apnea.
nasal-congestion.infections_text: The flu or acute sinusitis secondary to a common cold are caused by a viral infection. These viruses are airborne and cause inflammation of nasal tissues.
nasal-congestion.infections_extra: If the nasal mucosa turns yellow or green, it indicates that it has been complicated by a bacterial infection. Sinus infection also causes nasal congestion, headaches, irritated throat, cough, and general malaise.

nasal-congestion.structural_extra: Other structural causes: hypertrophied turbinates, nasal polyps, nasal valve collapse, crooked nose, and obstructive adenoids (common in children).
nasal-congestion.allergies_text: They occur due to the inflammatory response to harmless environmental substances (allergens) such as pollen, dust mites, household dust, pet dander, and tobacco smoke.
nasal-congestion.allergies_extra: These allergens release a substance called histamine that can cause congestion and excessive nasal mucus production.

nasal-obstruction.title_h1: Nasal Obstruction: Specialized Solutions to Improve Your Breathing
nasal-obstruction.intro_text: Nasal obstruction is a common symptom derived from various conditions that block, totally or partially, the airways. This condition manifests as if something restricts the airflow to breathe easily.
nasal-obstruction.causes_text: There are several factors that can compromise nasal function. Among the most common are:
nasal-obstruction.adenoids_text: They are glands located behind the nasal cavity. When inflamed, they narrow the respiratory passage, being the main cause of obstruction in children (although rare in adults).
nasal-obstruction.mucosa_text: Infections or allergies can inflame internal tissues. Conditions such as allergic rhinitis, vasomotor rhinitis, sinusitis, and nasal vestibulitis significantly restrict airflow.
nasal-obstruction.deviated_septum_text: The septum is the structure of bone and cartilage that divides the nose into two cavities. If crooked, it creates a fixed mechanical obstruction that does not respond to medication. In these cases, the only definitive solution is septoplasty.
nasal-obstruction.polyps_text: They are soft, non-cancerous growths in the lining of the nasal passages or sinuses that act as a physical barrier to air.
nasal-obstruction.turbinates_text: The inferior turbinates can excessively enlarge due to allergies or irritants. Although medical treatment helps, severe cases require surgical reduction.
nasal-obstruction.nasal_valve_text: The nasal valve is the narrowest area of the airway. If its walls are weak and collapse when inhaling, breathing becomes difficult.
nasal-obstruction.choanal_atresia_text: A congenital condition where babies are born with excess tissue blocking the nasal passages, requiring immediate attention.
nasal-obstruction.treatment_options_text: Depending on the diagnosis, there are two main approaches:
nasal-obstruction.non_invasive_text: Ideal for inflammatory or allergic processes:
nasal-obstruction.surgical_text: Indicated when there is a structural alteration:
nasal-obstruction.surgical_item3: Endoscopic nasal surgery: To remove polyps or treat chronic sinusitis.

nasal-obstruction.symptom3: In children: constant mouth breathing, which can lead to dental problems and facial development issues.

nasal-obstruction.septum_text: The nasal septum is the structure that divides the nasal cavities into the right and left sides. A deviated septum refers to a septum that is crooked.
nasal-obstruction.septum_note: Fixed obstruction that can only be corrected with surgery (septoplasty).
nasal-obstruction.turbinates_section_text: The turbinates are near the septum, but normally there is enough space between the septum and the turbinates to allow airflow.
nasal-obstruction.turbinates_section_note: Can improve with medication or allergy treatment.

snoring.seo_intro: Snoring is a sound produced by the vibration of tissues in the nose and throat during breathing while we sleep. When you breathe, air flows steadily in and out of the lungs. However, as you fall asleep and transition from light to deep sleep, the muscles of the palate, tongue, and throat relax enough to partially block the airway and begin to vibrate. The more the airway narrows, the greater the force generated by the airflow. This increases tissue vibration and produces louder snoring.
snoring.when_problem_title: When can it be a major problem?
snoring.when_problem_text: In some cases, snoring is associated with a sleep disorder called obstructive sleep apnea (OSA). Not everyone who snores has OSA; however, if snoring is accompanied by any of the following symptoms, a medical evaluation is important:
snoring.symptom6: Gasping or choking episodes at night
snoring.risk_factors_text: Several factors can contribute to the occurrence of snoring:
snoring.risk1: Alcohol consumption: Relaxes throat muscles and decreases natural defenses against obstruction.
snoring.risk2: Nasal problems: Chronic nasal congestion or a deviated septum contribute significantly.
snoring.risk3: Sleep deprivation: Not getting enough sleep causes greater relaxation of throat tissues.
snoring.risk4: Sleeping position: Snoring is more common when sleeping on your back, as gravity narrows the airway.
snoring.risk5: Anatomy and gender: Men have a higher predisposition. Also, a long palate, large tonsils, or adenoids can narrow the airway.
snoring.risk6: Overweight: Excess neck tissue increases pressure on the airway.
snoring.risk7: Family history: Genetics is a potential risk factor for OSA.
snoring.habit2: Avoid alcohol or sedative medications before bed.
snoring.habit4: Sleep on your side instead of your back.
snoring.dental_devices_text: These devices advance the jaw to keep the airway open. They are useful in mild cases or in patients who have not responded to lifestyle changes.
snoring.cpap_text: This device provides constant airflow through a mask, preventing the airway from collapsing during inhalation and exhalation. It is one of the most effective treatments for obstructive sleep apnea.
snoring.surgical_text: The goal of surgery is to improve airflow through the nose and correct anatomical abnormalities that contribute to obstruction.
snoring.procedure2: Nasal valvuloplasty: Improves nasal valve support.
snoring.procedure3: Cauterization or turbinate reduction: Decreases the size of tissues that block airflow.

throat.seo_h1: Throat Diseases: Guide to Causes, Symptoms, and Treatments
throat.seo_intro: The throat (pharynx) is a muscular tube-shaped conduit that connects the nasal and oral cavities with the esophagus and larynx. Its function is vital and dual: it allows food to pass into the digestive system and conducts air to the trachea for breathing. As the common entry point for air and food, the throat is particularly vulnerable to infections and other conditions. The most frequent causes of discomfort include viral or bacterial infections, allergies, and gastroesophageal reflux, which occurs when stomach acids flow back into the esophagus, irritating the area.
throat.common_sore_throat_text: Viruses, such as those responsible for the common cold or influenza (flu), are the main causes of sore throat. It is important to differentiate these conditions from a streptococcal (bacterial) infection, as treatment varies significantly. Generally, most sore throats improve spontaneously within a week.
throat.common_sore_throat_symptom2: Feeling of dryness or constant irritation
throat.common_sore_throat_note: Note: If you have a cough, runny nose, or hoarseness (whispered or raspy voice), the cause is very likely a virus and not bacteria.
throat.tonsillitis_seo_text: The tonsils, located at the back of the throat, are part of the lymphatic system. Their function is to trap bacteria and germs to prevent infections in the rest of the body. When they become infected by viruses or bacteria, tonsillitis occurs.
throat.tonsillitis_symptoms: Symptoms: Severe pain, difficulty swallowing, fever, visible redness, headache, and even nausea or ear pain.
throat.tonsillitis_treatment: Medical treatment: Use of analgesics (ibuprofen/acetaminophen), plenty of fluids, and if bacterial, antibiotics such as penicillin.
throat.tonsillitis_surgical: Surgical option: Tonsillectomy is reserved for chronic or severe cases.
throat.pharyngitis_seo_text: This is the specific inflammation of the pharynx. Although it shares symptoms with the common sore throat, it usually presents with more systemic symptoms.
throat.pharyngitis_symptoms: Additional symptoms: Muscle and joint pain, skin rashes, and swollen, tender lymph nodes in the neck.
throat.pharyngitis_treatment: Treatment: Focuses on fighting the infection (amoxicillin if bacterial) and relieving discomfort through salt water gargles and rest.
throat.throat_cancer_seo_text: The predominant risk factor for cancer of the larynx or pharynx is tobacco use (both smoked and smokeless) and chronic alcoholism. Other factors include advanced age and Human Papillomavirus (HPV).
throat.throat_cancer_warning: Warning signs: Presence of a lump that does not go away, persistent hoarseness, unexplained voice changes, and chronic ear pain.
throat.throat_cancer_diagnosis: Diagnosis: Performed through a complete clinical evaluation, specialized tests, and finally a biopsy.
throat.throat_cancer_treatment: Treatments: Depending on the stage, it may include radiotherapy, surgery (partial or total laryngectomy), or a combination of chemotherapy and radiation.
throat.croup_seo_text: Croup is an inflammation of the upper airways that primarily affects young children. It is characterized by a dry, strong cough, similar to a 'bark,' which usually worsens at night.
throat.when_to_see: When to see an ENT specialist? If the pain persists for more than a week, there is severe difficulty breathing, or the fever is very high, it is essential to see a specialist.

sleep-apnea.seo_intro: Sleep apnea is a serious disorder in which breathing repeatedly stops and starts, disrupting sleep. This interruption typically causes a drop in oxygen levels and an increase in carbon dioxide levels in the blood.
sleep-apnea.obstructive_text: occurs when the upper airway becomes blocked multiple times during sleep. It is caused by repeated closures of the throat or upper airway. The upper airway consists of the passage from the mouth and nasal openings to the throat and down to the larynx; these structures can change position when a person breathes. The blockage can reduce or completely stop airflow. This is the most common type of sleep apnea.
sleep-apnea.children_text: In children, enlarged tonsils or adenoids, certain dental conditions, obesity, and some congenital abnormalities can cause obstructive sleep apnea. Seasonal allergies causing significant nasal congestion can worsen the condition. Most affected children snore. Other sleep-related symptoms may include unrefreshing rest and night sweats. Daytime symptoms may include mouth breathing and concentration problems. Learning and behavioral problems (such as hyperactivity) are often common symptoms of severe obstructive sleep apnea in children. Growth delays may also occur.
sleep-apnea.central_text: occurs when the brain does not send the necessary signals to breathe. Health conditions that affect how the brain controls the airway and chest muscles can cause this type of apnea.
sleep-apnea.symptoms_text: In all types of sleep apnea, sleep disruptions can cause:
sleep-apnea.symptom6: The most common symptom is snoring, which tends to be disruptive, with episodes of gasping or choking, breathing pauses, and sudden awakenings with a snort. Affected individuals may wake up choking and frightened.
sleep-apnea.symptom7: In the morning, patients are often unaware that their sleep has been interrupted many times. Some wake up with a sore throat or dry mouth.
sleep-apnea.symptom8: When obstructive apnea is severe, repeated episodes of snorting and loud snoring occur at night, and during the day the person feels sleepy or even falls asleep unintentionally.
sleep-apnea.risk_factors_text: The likelihood of developing obstructive sleep apnea increases due to various factors. Obesity, combined with aging and other elements, leads to narrowing of the upper airway. Excessive alcohol consumption and use of sedatives worsen the condition. Having a narrow throat or thick neck (traits that tend to be similar among family members) indicates that, in most cases, the condition tends to be hereditary. Low thyroid hormone levels (hypothyroidism), nighttime gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD), or excessive growth due to overproduction of growth hormone (acromegaly) contribute to this type of apnea. In some cases, a stroke can also cause it. If left untreated, it can lead to complications such as hypertension, heart failure, heart rhythm disorders, atherosclerotic heart disease, pulmonary hypertension, insulin resistance, and even death.
sleep-apnea.diagnosis_text: Doctors diagnose obstructive sleep apnea when the following occur:
sleep-apnea.diagnosis2: There are 5 or more breathing interruptions per hour.
sleep-apnea.diagnosis3: Each interruption lasts more than 10 seconds.
sleep-apnea.dental_text: Dental devices that advance the jaw forward can be used for mild snoring and in people who have not responded to behavioral changes.
sleep-apnea.nasal1: Adhesive nasal strips to enlarge nasal passages
sleep-apnea.cpap_text: Continuous Positive Airway Pressure (CPAP) is a device that prevents airway narrowing during inhalation and exhalation, providing increased persistent pressure.
sleep-apnea.surgery_text: May be necessary to correct anatomical abnormalities:
sleep-apnea.surgery1: Septoplasty: correction of deviated nasal septum.
sleep-apnea.reason1: Increased energy level: With proper treatment, you will achieve deeper, uninterrupted sleep.
sleep-apnea.reason2: Improved mood: By treating apnea, you may experience emotional stabilization, feeling more balanced in daily life.
sleep-apnea.reason3: Reduction of daytime headaches: By improving nighttime oxygenation, there is a high probability of eliminating these headaches.
sleep-apnea.reason4: Prevention of heart problems: Treatment helps reduce risks of hypertension, heart failure, and arrhythmias, protecting heart health.
sleep-apnea.suspicion_text: Untreated apnea can have serious consequences. If you experience these symptoms, consult Dr. Lumbán for a complete evaluation and the most appropriate treatment for your specific case.

voice-disorders.seo_h1: Voice Disorders: Diagnosis and Specialized Treatment
voice-disorders.seo_intro: The voice is a fundamental tool for our communication and personal expression. It is produced when air from the lungs passes through the larynx, causing the vocal cords to vibrate and generate sound. However, when this delicate mechanism is altered, voice disorders arise. Dr. Jaime Lumban specializes in vocal health recovery, using cutting-edge technology to treat various conditions.
voice-disorders.classification_text: Voice problems are not all the same. They are divided into three main categories:
voice-disorders.organic: Organic: Caused by alterations in the structure of the larynx or vocal cords (such as nodules or inflammation).
voice-disorders.neurological: Neurological: Occur when the nerves that control the larynx do not function correctly.
voice-disorders.functional: Functional: Appear when structures are normal, but the use of vocal muscles is inefficient or incorrect, often aggravated by stress or emotional factors.
voice-disorders.common_types_title: Most common types of voice disorders
voice-disorders.common_types_text: Among the conditions that most frequently alter the voice are:
voice-disorders.nodules: Vocal nodules: Small benign growths on the vocal cords, usually associated with excessive or incorrect voice use.
voice-disorders.polyps: Vocal polyps: Benign lesions that appear as swelling or mass on one or both vocal cords.
voice-disorders.laryngitis: Laryngitis: Inflammation or irritation of the vocal cords, usually caused by respiratory infections, allergies, or reflux irritation.
voice-disorders.muscle_tension: Muscle tension dysphonia: Occurs when the laryngeal muscles become excessively tense. It can cause pain when speaking and also affect the neck, shoulders, and upper back.
voice-disorders.spasmodic: Spasmodic dysphonia (laryngeal dystonia): A neurological disorder that causes involuntary spasms in the vocal cords, altering voice sound.
voice-disorders.benign_lesions: Benign vocal cord lesions: Include cysts, nodules, or polyps that affect normal vocal cord vibration.
voice-disorders.paralysis: Vocal cord paralysis: Occurs when one or both vocal cords do not move correctly, affecting breathing, voice, or swallowing.
voice-disorders.causes_text: The larynx is made up of muscles, soft tissues, and the vocal cords, located at the top of the trachea. When these structures become inflamed, injured, or fail to move properly, the voice can be altered. Among the most common causes are:
voice-disorders.when_to_see_title: When to see Dr. Jaime Lumban?
voice-disorders.when_to_see_text: If you notice changes in your voice that persist for more than two weeks, it is important to have an evaluation. Warning symptoms include:
voice-disorders.alert2: Changes in pitch (very high or very low)
voice-disorders.alert5: Fatigue or pain when speaking, feeling of a lump in the throat.
voice-disorders.alert6: Loss of high notes in singers.
voice-disorders.alert7: Sudden interruptions or breaks in sound.
voice-disorders.diagnosis_text: To identify the exact cause, Dr. Lumban will analyze symptoms, medical history, and perform a detailed examination of the head, neck, and throat. He will use advanced technology:
voice-disorders.laryngoscopy: Laryngoscopy: Evaluation with a high-resolution flexible endoscope.
voice-disorders.videostroboscopy: Videostroboscopy: A specialized study that allows observation of vocal cord vibration in slow motion, essential for accurate diagnosis.
voice-disorders.imaging: Imaging Studies: In specific cases, CT scans or MRIs may be requested.
voice-disorders.risk_factors_text: Some conditions or habits may increase the risk of developing voice disorders:
voice-disorders.risk4: Neurological diseases (such as Parkinson's or stroke sequelae)
voice-disorders.high_risk_professions_text: People who use their voice intensively are more likely to develop voice problems, for example:
voice-disorders.profession5: Professionals who speak constantly in public
voice-disorders.prevention_text: Some recommendations for vocal health care include:
voice-disorders.prevention1: Avoid tobacco and excessive alcohol consumption
voice-disorders.prevention3: Rest your voice when used for prolonged periods
voice-disorders.prevention4: Avoid shouting or straining your voice
voice-disorders.prevention5: Promptly treat respiratory infections and allergies

pediatric-ent.seo_h1: Pediatric ENT: Specialized Care for Ear, Nose, and Throat
pediatric-ent.seo_intro: Children and adolescents are not simply "small adults." Their bodies are constantly growing and their immune system is still developing. Therefore, for ear, nose, and throat conditions, they require differential diagnosis and treatment. At Dr. Lumbán's practice, we understand that medication dosing, interpreting non-verbal cues in young children, and observing acute or chronic conditions are fundamental pillars. We work hand in hand with the family and their primary care pediatrician to ensure healthy growth.
pediatric-ent.tonsils_adenoids_title: Tonsils and Adenoids: The Guardians of Immunity
pediatric-ent.tonsils_adenoids_text: The tonsils and adenoids are part of your child's immune system. They produce antibodies to help the body fight infections. However, when these tissues become infected or grow too large, they can cause significant problems.
pediatric-ent.tonsillitis_symptom1: Red, swollen tonsils with white or yellow patches.
pediatric-ent.tonsillitis_symptom4: Swollen lymph nodes in the neck and fever.
pediatric-ent.when_to_see_tonsils_title: When to see an ENT for tonsils?
pediatric-ent.when_to_see_tonsils_text: Difficulty breathing, breathing pauses at night, daytime sleepiness, refusal to eat due to pain, persistent high fever
pediatric-ent.pediatric_apnea_text: If your child snores frequently, it could be a warning sign. When tonsils are enlarged, muscles relax during deep sleep and block the airway.
pediatric-ent.what_happens_text: Frequent snoring that may hide episodes of partial or complete airway closure during sleep due to enlarged tonsils/adenoids.
pediatric-ent.consequences_text: Fragmented sleep → daytime fatigue, irritability, difficulties in school performance, and in severe cases, growth disorders.
pediatric-ent.solution_text: The solution: A detailed evaluation by an ENT specialist. In many cases, tonsil and adenoid removal is the ideal treatment.
pediatric-ent.ear_health_title: Hearing Health and Ear Infections and Ventilation Tubes
pediatric-ent.ear_health_text: Middle ear infections (otitis media) occur when bacteria or viruses infect the space behind the eardrum. Children are more susceptible because their Eustachian tubes are shorter, narrower, and more horizontal, which facilitates fluid accumulation.
pediatric-ent.ear_infection_symptoms_title: How do I know if my child has an ear infection?
pediatric-ent.ear_symptom1: Severe pain: Usually worsens at night.
pediatric-ent.ear_symptom2: Hearing problems: The child seems not to hear well or does not respond when called.
pediatric-ent.ear_symptom3: Drainage: Discharge of fluid or pus from the ear canal.
pediatric-ent.ventilation_tubes_title: Ventilation Tubes: When are they necessary?
pediatric-ent.ventilation_tubes_text: Indicated for recurrent otitis or persistent fluid causing hearing loss and language delay.
pediatric-ent.tube_types: Types: short-term (fall out on their own ~6–12 months) or long-term (require removal).
pediatric-ent.procedure_text: Procedure: myringotomy (minimal incision in the eardrum), suction of fluid, and tube insertion; takes minutes and is outpatient.
pediatric-ent.allergies_title: Allergies and Respiratory Problems in children
pediatric-ent.allergic_rhinitis_text: Unlike the common cold, rhinitis does not cause fever. It manifests with dark circles under the eyes, intense itching in the nose or palate, and frequent sneezing. Treatment must be personalized, including modern antihistamines that do not cause drowsiness or specific nasal sprays.
pediatric-ent.sinusitis_vs_cold_title: Differences between sinusitis and cold in children:
pediatric-ent.fever_cold: Uncommon or only at the beginning.
pediatric-ent.pain_sinusitis: Intense pain around the eyes and bad breath.
pediatric-ent.recommendation1: Record fever episodes, duration of pain, sleep patterns, and any changes in language or behavior.
pediatric-ent.recommendation2: Keep vaccinations and pediatric check-ups up to date.
pediatric-ent.recommendation3: Avoid exposure to tobacco smoke and environments with known allergens.
pediatric-ent.recommendation4: Seek ENT evaluation if there are recurrent infections, hearing loss, persistent snoring, or speech delay.
pediatric-ent.specialist_care_text: We have equipped facilities and cutting-edge technological equipment to treat all areas of pediatric otolaryngology. Our approach is preventive and minimally invasive, always prioritizing the comfort and peace of mind of our youngest patients.
pediatric-ent.final_cta: Do you notice that your child breathes through their mouth or has frequent infections? Timely diagnosis is the key to uncomplicated development.

endoscopic-surgery.what_is_sinusitis_text: Sinusitis is the inflammation of the mucous membrane that lines the inside of the nose and paranasal sinuses. The paranasal sinuses are bony cavities located in the skull, around the eyes and nose, whose main function is to produce mucus to clean and humidify the inspired air. When these mucous membranes become inflamed, edema (swelling) occurs and mucus production increases. This obstructs the natural drainage of the sinuses into the nose and throat. When retained, the mucus facilitates the proliferation of bacteria and viruses, leading to infection. Factors such as allergies and nasal polyps can also obstruct these pathways and chronicle the process.
endoscopic-surgery.sinusitis_types_text: There are two main forms of sinusitis:
endoscopic-surgery.chronic_criteria: Chronic sinusitis is considered when, for at least 12 weeks, the person presents at least two of the following symptoms:
endoscopic-surgery.chronic_symptom2: Pain or feeling of pressure in the face or head.
endoscopic-surgery.chronic_note: Additionally, there must be evidence of inflammation in the paranasal sinuses observed by the physician or on a computed tomography (CT) scan.
endoscopic-surgery.symptom1: Facial pain or feeling of heaviness.
endoscopic-surgery.non_surgical_treatment_text: In most cases, sinusitis improves with medical treatment, which may include: antibiotics (when appropriate), anti-inflammatories, antihistamines, decongestants, allergy treatment, and environmental measures (for example, avoiding smoking). The type of treatment is decided after medical evaluation to address the underlying cause.
endoscopic-surgery.surgery_indication_text: If sinusitis does not respond to appropriate medical measures or if there are anatomical alterations that hinder drainage (polyps, septal deviation, or other causes), endoscopic sinus surgery may be the indicated option.
endoscopic-surgery.surgical_procedure_text: Endoscopic surgery is a minimally invasive procedure that allows surgery through the nasal passages without the need for external incisions, thus avoiding visible scars.
endoscopic-surgery.duration: Duration: Between 1 and 3 hours, depending on complexity.
endoscopic-surgery.technique: Technique: High-resolution endoscopes with different viewing angles are used to visualize lesions with great precision and magnification.
endoscopic-surgery.advantage3: Outpatient procedure (discharged the same day in most cases).
endoscopic-surgery.post_op_title: Recommendations for the first 3 to 4 days:
endoscopic-surgery.rest: Relative rest: Maintain a sitting or semi-sitting position to reduce cephalic pressure and bleeding.
endoscopic-surgery.restrictions: Restrictions: Do not drink alcohol, do not smoke, do not drive, and avoid any physical exertion.
endoscopic-surgery.diet: Diet: Soft, cold, or room temperature foods are recommended, as well as plenty of hydration to relieve throat dryness caused by mouth breathing.
endoscopic-surgery.hygiene: Hygiene: It is essential not to blow your nose.
endoscopic-surgery.medications: Medications: Analgesics/anti-inflammatories will be prescribed for discomfort and antibiotics to prevent infections.
endoscopic-surgery.packing_removal: Packing removal: Performed in the office between 2 and 6 days later. If nasal splints were placed, they are removed between the first and third week.
endoscopic-surgery.nasal_washes: Nasal washes: Essential during the first weeks to clean crusts and secretions, facilitating healing.
endoscopic-surgery.return_activity: Return to activity: The patient can resume normal activities in 1 or 2 weeks, but should avoid intense physical exercise for one month.
endoscopic-surgery.final_cta_title: Do you have questions about endoscopic sinus surgery?
endoscopic-surgery.final_cta_text: For a personalized diagnosis or to clarify any concerns, Dr. Lumbán is at your disposal. You can schedule an appointment through our phone number or via email. Your respiratory health is our priority.

anti-snoring-surgery.seo_h1: Anti-Snoring Surgery with Dr. Jaime Lumbán: Sleep Disorder Expert in Tijuana
anti-snoring-surgery.snoring_surgical_text: Snoring is a common symptom within the spectrum of sleep breathing disorders, which usually occurs independently or associated with sleep apnea syndrome, learn more at: drlumban.com/sleep-apnea. This symptom can significantly affect sleep quality and overall health. In many cases, it is associated with upper airway obstruction, soft palate vibration, or increased pharyngeal tissue. When snoring is persistent or accompanied by breathing pauses, a complete evaluation is important to define the appropriate treatment.
anti-snoring-surgery.surgery_areas_text: Sleep apnea or snoring surgeries are divided into three main areas: nasal, palate, and tongue regions, in order to reduce obstructions and widen the airways. More than one intervention in the area may be required.
anti-snoring-surgery.surgery_types_text: Each patient is unique, as is their diagnosis. Therefore, some approaches will be more convenient than others depending on age, lifestyle, and general physiognomy. Some surgical approaches for snoring are:
anti-snoring-surgery.radiofrequency_text: Also known as cold ablation, it can be performed in the nasal, palate, tongue, and epiglottis regions. This radiofrequency technology uses ions and a specialized probe to intentionally form scar tissue, which stabilizes the area and makes it less prone to vibrate or block airflow.
anti-snoring-surgery.uvulopalatopharyngoplasty_text: This is a surgery performed to open the upper airway by removing excess tissue at the back of the throat. This includes:
anti-snoring-surgery.upfp_item1: All or part of the uvula (the soft tissue that hangs at the back of the mouth).
anti-snoring-surgery.upfp_item2: Parts of the palate and soft tissue on the sides of the throat.
anti-snoring-surgery.upfp_item3: The tonsils and adenoids (if they have not been previously removed).
anti-snoring-surgery.upfp_recovery: Recovery: The estimated complete recovery time is 2 to 3 weeks.
anti-snoring-surgery.nasal_valve_text: It is an area in each nostril that plays an important role in air aspiration. This area, just a few millimeters, is considered by specialists as a key element of breathing, even more important than the septum or turbinates.
anti-snoring-surgery.nasal_valvuloplasty_text: The intervention is performed inside the nostril and leaves no visible external scars. Before the procedure, a thorough examination is necessary to evaluate the patient's general health. It is worth mentioning that this surgery can slightly widen the nasal bridge to allow greater airflow; Dr. Lumbán will provide functional and aesthetic results.
anti-snoring-surgery.septoplasty_text: Septoplasty: Straightens the septum (the wall that divides the nostrils) when it is deviated. It is also used to remove bone growths called septal spurs. Read more about this at https://drlumban.com/septoplasty/
anti-snoring-surgery.turbinate_reduction_text: Turbinate reduction: Removes excess tissue around the turbinate bones to facilitate airflow. It can be performed independently or combined with a septoplasty or rhinoplasty.
anti-snoring-surgery.diagnosis_text: Dr. Lumbán performs a comprehensive evaluation of the upper airway that includes medical history, physical examination, and specialized studies such as nasofibroscopy. The latter is a fiber optic study that allows examination of the deep structures of the nose, throat, and larynx.
anti-snoring-surgery.nasofibroscopy_title: Nasofibroscopy is commonly used in the diagnosis of:
anti-snoring-surgery.nasofibroscopy_item5: Nodules, cysts, or polyps on vocal cords
anti-snoring-surgery.polysomnography_text: In specific cases, a polysomnography is requested to accurately measure sleep quality and quantify the presence of apnea.
anti-snoring-surgery.final_cta_title: Do you have questions about which anti-snoring surgery is ideal for you?
anti-snoring-surgery.final_cta_text: Schedule a consultation with Dr. Lumbán for a complete evaluation.

microscopic-surgery.seo_h1: Microscopic Laryngeal Surgery: Treatment for Vocal Cord Lesions
microscopic-surgery.seo_intro: Voice changes can be the first symptom of something more serious, such as vocal weakness, vocal cord tumors, or even throat cancer. If you have hoarseness, discomfort, or voice changes lasting more than three weeks, it is recommended to see an ENT specialist who can examine the larynx and determine the cause of the problem. The vocal cords are located in the larynx and voice is the result of these structures vibrating. Any irregularity or mass on the vocal cords can alter their vibration and consequently cause voice changes.
microscopic-surgery.what_is_text: Microscopic laryngeal surgery, also known as microlaryngoscopy, is a procedure that allows evaluation and removal of various vocal cord lesions, including: Cancer, cysts, papillomas, polyps, and Reinke's edema.
microscopic-surgery.non_surgical_title: Non-surgical vocal cord treatment and vocal cord surgery
microscopic-surgery.non_surgical_text: Most voice problems can be successfully treated with non-invasive methods:
microscopic-surgery.surgical_treatment_title: Sometimes voice disorders require direct intervention:
microscopic-surgery.surgical_item2: Removal of lesions (cysts, polyps, or nodules).
microscopic-surgery.surgical_item3: Biopsy of suspicious lesions for diagnosis.
microscopic-surgery.diseases_title: Vocal Cord Diseases That May Require Surgery
microscopic-surgery.nodules_text: Often called "singer's nodules," these are benign growths that develop due to excessive strain or misuse of the voice. Patients may experience hoarseness, a breathy voice, or vocal fatigue. When conservative treatments like voice therapy do not produce improvement, surgery may be indicated.
microscopic-surgery.polyps_text: Like nodules, polyps are benign lesions that can cause voice changes and discomfort. They are generally related to vocal abuse or trauma. If polyps are large or persistent, laryngeal microsurgery may be necessary to remove them.
microscopic-surgery.cysts_text: These fluid-filled sacs can form on the vocal cords and cause hoarseness or voice changes. Surgery is often required to remove the cyst and restore normal vocal function.
microscopic-surgery.tumors_text: Benign or malignant tumors can occur in the larynx. In these cases, a biopsy may be performed to determine the nature of the tumor. If malignancy or cancer risk is confirmed, laryngeal microsurgery may be essential for removal and subsequent treatment.
microscopic-surgery.paralysis_text: This condition can be caused by various factors, such as nerve damage or injury. In some cases, surgery can help reposition the vocal cords or improve their function, helping to improve voice and airway management.
microscopic-surgery.stenosis_text: This is a narrowing of the airway below the vocal cords, which can cause difficulty breathing. Laryngeal microsurgery can help widen the airway and improve airflow.
microscopic-surgery.inflammation_text: Chronic inflammation or swelling of the larynx can cause voice changes and discomfort. In some cases, surgery may be necessary to treat the underlying cause and restore normal function.
microscopic-surgery.preparation_title: Preparation and Diagnosis for Laryngeal Surgery
microscopic-surgery.preoperative_text: It is recommended to schedule a consultation with Dr. Lumbán, ENT specialist. During this appointment, your medical history will be reviewed, a physical examination will be performed, and the procedure, possible risks, and expected outcomes will be explained.
microscopic-surgery.diagnostic_tests_text: Before surgery, Dr. Lumbán may request studies such as:
microscopic-surgery.test1: Laryngoscopy: a procedure that allows visualization of the larynx and assessment of its condition.
microscopic-surgery.test2: Imaging studies: CT scan or MRI to analyze the extent of the problem.
microscopic-surgery.test3: Blood tests: routine laboratory tests to identify possible underlying health conditions.
microscopic-surgery.how_performed_title: How is Vocal Cord Surgery Performed?
microscopic-surgery.how_performed_text: Vocal cord surgery is performed using direct laryngoscopy (microlaryngoscopy) under general anesthesia. While the patient is deeply asleep, a metal laryngoscope is used to displace the tongue and allow clear vision. Using a high-precision microscope, the surgeon obtains a magnified view of the vocal cords. Using specialized instruments or laser technology, the condition is treated. The main goal is to resect the lesion as precisely as possible, minimizing impact on surrounding healthy tissue to preserve voice quality.
microscopic-surgery.recovery_item1: Most laryngeal surgeries are performed on an outpatient basis.
microscopic-surgery.recovery_item2: Voice rest is recommended during the first few days after surgery.
microscopic-surgery.recovery_item3: Many patients can return to work approximately after one week.
microscopic-surgery.recovery_item4: Voice improvement usually occurs gradually over several weeks.
microscopic-surgery.recovery_text: It is essential to stay well hydrated and avoid speaking as much as possible to allow proper healing of the vocal cords. Using humidifiers to keep the air moist is also recommended, which can help soothe the throat. After the first week, many patients begin to notice improvements in their voice quality and overall well-being. However, complete recovery may take several weeks, so it is important to attend follow-up appointments with the surgeon to monitor the healing process.

microscopic-surgery.final_cta_text: We invite you to schedule an evaluation with Dr. Lumbán, an expert in voice disorders and minimally invasive surgery.

rhinoplasty.seo_h1: Aesthetic Nose Surgery: Perfect Balance Between Aesthetics and Nasal Function
rhinoplasty.seo_intro_suffix: years of experience, Dr. Jaime Lumbán has dedicated himself to perfecting aesthetic and functional nose surgery. Although it may seem like a simple structure, nasal anatomy is extremely complex and demands absolute precision. Factors such as cartilage resistance and skin type vary in each patient; therefore, what works for one person is not always ideal for another. The approach of an otolaryngologist is to seek results that harmonize with the face and enhance natural beauty, always maintaining respiratory function as the fundamental pillar of each intervention.
rhinoplasty.what_is_text: It is the surgery designed to give a new shape to the nose. Through this procedure, it is possible to increase or reduce its size, change the nasal angle, refine the tip, or correct bumps and deviations.
rhinoplasty.dorsal_hump_title: Reduction of the dorsal hump or nasal bridge
rhinoplasty.dorsal_hump_text: The nasal bridge is the bone that runs from the area between the eyebrows to the tip of the nose. When there is a protuberance or 'hump,' it can be reduced and smoothed to create a more harmonious and straight profile. In some nose types — such as Asian or African noses — cartilage grafts may be necessary to improve nasal bridge projection.
rhinoplasty.tip_refinement_text: The nasal tip is one of the areas that most influences facial harmony. Refinement is performed by modifying the nasal cartilages and the nasolabial angle, which allows: projecting the tip forward, improving definition, achieving a more balanced and refined profile.
rhinoplasty.base_reduction_text: Surgery can also focus on reducing the width of the nasal alae, correcting disproportions and improving facial balance. A previous rhinoplasty and have subsequent breathing problems or want additional changes in the appearance of the nose. These cases are considerably more difficult and seeing a rhinoplasty specialist is a necessity.
rhinoplasty.functional_text: Performed on patients with respiratory problems, generally due to: deviated nasal septum (septum), nasal bone deformities, chronic nasal obstruction. Indicated for patients with breathing difficulties caused by deviated septum, bone deformities, or hypertrophy due to allergies. Functional correction usually brings with it a notable improvement in external appearance.
rhinoplasty.aesthetic_text: Focused on patients who wish to exclusively improve the shape of their nose. Dr. Lumbán ensures that the aesthetic change never sacrifices the ability to breathe properly.
rhinoplasty.revision_text: For those who have undergone previous surgery and have breathing problems or dissatisfaction with visual results. These cases are highly complex and require the experience of a specialist.
rhinoplasty.approaches_text: Depending on each case, the method that guarantees the best results and a more comfortable recovery is selected:
rhinoplasty.closed_text: Performed exclusively through the nostrils, leaving no external scars. It is ideal for less invasive modifications, as it allows access to the internal structure with less impact on surrounding tissues.
rhinoplasty.open_text: A minimal incision is made in the columella (the base that separates the nostrils). This technique offers a direct and complete view of the nasal structure, being the preferred option for complex or revision cases where extreme precision is vital. The resulting scar is practically invisible over time.
rhinoplasty.ultrasonic_text: Thanks to ultrasonic technology, it is possible to make precise cuts in the nasal bone, which allows: reducing tissue trauma, decreasing bleeding, avoiding aggressive fractures, improving postoperative recovery. This type of technique can also allow surgeries without the use of nasal packing, making the recovery process more comfortable for the patient.
rhinoplasty.final_cta_title: What type of rhinoplasty is best for you?
rhinoplasty.final_cta_text: Each nose is unique, so the best technique depends on your anatomy, your aesthetic goals, and your respiratory function. sinusitis-surgery.seo_h1: Sinusitis Surgery: Definitive Treatment for Chronic Sinusitis
sinusitis-surgery.seo_intro: Chronic sinusitis affects millions of people who, despite multiple medical treatments, continue to suffer from nasal congestion, facial pain, thick discharge, and loss of smell. When antibiotics, corticosteroids, and nasal washes are not enough, endoscopic sinus surgery becomes the best option to regain quality of life.
sinusitis-surgery.indication_text: Surgery is not the first step, but it is recommended when:
sinusitis-surgery.indication1: Symptoms persist for more than 12 weeks despite adequate medical treatment.
sinusitis-surgery.indication2: Nasal polyps are blocking sinus drainage.
sinusitis-surgery.indication3: There are recurrent infections (more than 4 episodes per year).
sinusitis-surgery.indication4: Complications such as ocular or neurological involvement occur.
sinusitis-surgery.indication5: Imaging studies (CT scan) show significant anatomical obstruction.
sinusitis-surgery.fess_text: It is the gold standard procedure. It is performed through the nostrils with a high-definition endoscope, without external incisions or scars. The goal is to enlarge the natural sinus openings to restore drainage and ventilation.
sinusitis-surgery.balloon_text: A minimally invasive technique where a catheter with a balloon is inserted and inflated to dilate obstructed openings. It is ideal for patients with chronic sinusitis without polyps or complex anatomy. Recovery is faster with less discomfort.
sinusitis-surgery.polypectomy_text: Nasal polyps are soft, non-cancerous growths that block the sinuses. Their removal dramatically improves breathing and sense of smell. It is usually combined with FESS for better results.
sinusitis-surgery.recovery_title: What is recovery like after surgery?
sinusitis-surgery.recovery_text: Recovery is a gradual but manageable process:
sinusitis-surgery.early_days3: Apply cold compresses to reduce swelling.
sinusitis-surgery.first_week1: Frequent nasal washes with saline solution.
sinusitis-surgery.first_week2: Avoid physical exertion and heavy lifting.
sinusitis-surgery.first_week4: Follow-up with Dr. Lumbán for endoscopic cleaning.
sinusitis-surgery.why_doctor_title: Why choose Dr. Jaime Lumbán for your sinusitis surgery?
sinusitis-surgery.why_doctor_experience: years of experience in otolaryngology, Dr. Lumbán is a reference in endoscopic sinus surgery in Tijuana. His approach combines:
sinusitis-surgery.why_doctor1: Minimally invasive techniques with cutting-edge technology.
sinusitis-surgery.why_doctor2: Personalized care focused on each patient's needs.
sinusitis-surgery.why_doctor3: Rigorous postoperative follow-up to ensure optimal results.
sinusitis-surgery.why_doctor4: Outpatient procedures that allow you to go home the same day.
sinusitis-surgery.faq_title: Frequently asked questions about sinusitis surgery
sinusitis-surgery.faq1_a: Surgery is performed under general anesthesia, so no pain is felt during the procedure. In the postoperative period, discomfort is mild and easily controlled with common analgesics.
sinusitis-surgery.faq2_q: How long does the surgery take?
sinusitis-surgery.faq2_a: Duration varies depending on complexity, but generally ranges from 1 to 3 hours.
sinusitis-surgery.faq3_q: When can I return to work?
sinusitis-surgery.faq3_a: Depending on the type of work, 3 to 7 days of rest is recommended for office jobs, and 2 to 3 weeks for demanding physical activities.
sinusitis-surgery.faq4_a: In most cases, results are permanent. However, patients with severe allergies or nasal polyps may require long-term complementary treatments.
sinusitis-surgery.faq5_a: It depends on each policy. Many insurances cover surgery when indicated for chronic sinusitis refractory to medical treatment.
sinusitis-surgery.final_cta_text: If you have tried multiple treatments for sinusitis without success, endoscopic surgery may be the solution you need. Don't let chronic nasal congestion limit your life.
